commentary: lbw appeal first ball! But Kumar Dharmasena is unmoved. Pitches on a good length, zips along with the arm. Roy seems a bit nervous on that. Slow to bring the bat towards it. Would have missed leg
pre_text:
Sammy is doling out some towels - perhaps worried about the dew. Then they go into a huddle. DJ Bravo's talking first though. A few claps follow and a loud roar greets England openers Jason Roy and Alex Hales. Eden Gardens is geed up for this. Judging by the 1000-plus words I've typed, maybe so am I. Samuel Badree, that legspinner Powerplay specialist, has the new ball. He has played 28 T20Is, he's opened the bowling every single time. Slip in place

6.53 pm The teams are on the edge of the boundary peeling their hair off looking uber cool. They stride out now for the national anthems, but first they have to negotiate a line of fireworks going off in their faces. First up, Rally 'round the West Indies, then God save the Queen. Sammy has this contented smile on his face, as if this is where he is supposed to be, as if this is his time. A cry of "Barmy Army" is heard before England's anthem and solemn faces come up on screen. Young team, Stokes, Root, Willey, Roy, lots ahead of them. 

There I was, scouring for content to shove down ahem, treat you lovely people and in comes Sid Monga from Kolkata to save the day. (He left the cape back in the press box) "The stands are about two-thirds full, which is surprising." And at Eden Gardens, which can host close to 70,000 people, that is saying something! 

Najam: "Don't forget, in IPL this is also the home ground of Eoin Morgan :)"

Hemant: "Who would have thought that after 34 games, there would be no Asian team in the finale! Surely, I did not."

"Last Time it was a Simmon show all the way as he was playing on his IPL Homeground. So can we expect the Same from Andre Russell Tonight ??" ----- Mustafa Moudi brings you TrendzWatch, with a Z. Cause this is T20. 

"Both teams are pretty similar ,very good batting unit, great bowling at death ,good at chase so its all about keeping nerves calm at right moment and get over the line." ----- Sanketp45, who do you think England football star Harry Kane is supporting? Here's a clue

6.33 pm Finally, out walk the captains - Sammy with his hand around Morgan, both with big smiles on their face, and the match referee Ranjan Madugalle for the toss. Morgan will spin, Sammy calls heads, and it is a head! West Indies are going to bowl "At the end of the day, we want the fans to be entertained and we come out victories. No changes. We came into this tournament with a lot of confidence. Not many gave us a chance, but we knew what we could do. Today we just have to take one more step. I said we have 15 match-winners. So far somebody has taken responsibility to take the team home. We've been inspired by the Under-19 boys and seeing the women be victorious, we are inspired"

"Would have had a bowl first," says Morgan, "Looks a really good surface. Big covering of grass, normally its quite bare and takes a bit of turn. Unchanged as well. I think in all three facets of the game, we've grown in confidence. [On Gayle] As much as we did before any team meeting, its important to stress we dont focus on one player. The India semi-final proved that"

Oh, by the way, it would seem Sammy has won his 10th toss in a row. #GoldenArm. Bharath Seervi also chimes in with, "Sammy has won the toss in all the 6 matches of this #WT20 and has elected to bowl first everytime!"

LVS: "I had trouble deciding whom to root for. The thing I hate the most about cricket is the result of the match being skewed by the toss. So I've decided to root for England."

England 1 Jason Roy, 2 Alex Hales, 3 Joe Root, 4 Eoin Morgan (capt), 5 Jos Buttler (wk), 6 Ben Stokes, 7 Moeen Ali, 8 Chris Jordan, 9 Adil Rashid, 10 David Willey, 11 Liam Plunkett

West Indies 1 Chris Gayle, 2 Johnson Charles, 3 Lendl Simmons, 4 Marlon Samuels, 5 Denesh Ramdin (wk), 6 Dwayne Bravo, 7 Andre Russell, 8 Darren Sammy (capt), 9 Carlos Brathwaite, 10 Sulieman Benn, 11 Samuel Badree

"It's not a good-looking surface," the pitch report says. How Rude! "Little discolored. Green grass on one side, brown grass as well. Footmarks from the women's match as well. It won't be a turner. It should under lights slide on. It's a decent surface. It will all come down to execution." 


Today is your last chance to win CricIQ! Head over here to take the quiz. Also, Sid Monga reports, "The ladies' press conferences are going on, the teams are warming up, there is a dance show on at the far end of the ground, and the stands are filling up. The weather is clear, there is thankfully a breeze to cool it down a little." 

Kartik: "Last day of the tournament....I have a little quiz here too.....How many wickets did Boult and Southee take in this event? :)" ----- Ohhh, ooohhh, I know this one. I know this one. Boy, that's going to be a doozy of a trick question in the lead up to the World T20 5016. I hope I can be on comms for that too. 

Dr. Arsalan: "I like B Stokes, and want to salute him for a purpose. #YouKnowWhatIMean" ----- #AndForThoseWhoDon't. These guys and their celebrations...

"While England doing so well this time is the result of their changed attitude and approach to Limited Overs Cricket post their ignominious exit in ICC WC'15, I still don't understand how they managed to win the WT20 in 2010." ---- Magic, LVS. KP, Collingwood and all the rest just went Abracadabra. #BetterThanSwitchHits

6.15 pm Stop the press! Match Day is upon us. Well, the match day is upon us, but so is Match Day, with Ian Chappell, Mahela Jayawardene and Ajit Agarkar. People on the web can simply refresh the scorecard and tune in to the pretty moving pictures on the top right of the page. For those on the app, open this trap door and fall down the rabbit hole. Don't forget to collect your parachutes from Gaurav Kalra. 

Cricket simplet: "Come on.. Its quite straight forward.. England gonna win.. Even stats will suggest that.. If windies are like CSK, eng are like MI.. the underdogs always win in india.. I really wish WI Not to bat first in this track to avoid an one sided final.. But my score against my wishes are 0-3.."

Faizii: "I supported PAK in the beginning, they lost, then supported SAF they lost then NZ they also lost and then IND unfortunately they are also out.. And now I am confused who to cheer for as both the teams are very good "

Vikram: "Mind:West Indies Heart:England for the enterprising brand of cricket they are playing."

"All said about pitch, high score, chasing, batsman's night, small boundaries - Benn & Badree's bowling will make the difference! It's WI bowling that can make a difference today" Gan, you'll be pleased to note that no less a cricket mind than Tony Cozier, that man with an encyclopedic knowledge of West Indies cricket, thinks along the same lines. Read his column here. 

6.00 pm "Let's be honest, Alagappan," Oh, but that is generally boring. But okay, Mark, "Whoever wins the toss will almost certainly win the match. The West Indies have chased every game and will chase again, if they can and England are also far happier chasing. With the dew, the side winning the toss will have a huge advantage." ---- It has been more or less true. Even New Zealand's inspired run in the league stages also involved them winning four tosses in a row. And the coin will be going up in just about half an hours time. Ooooh, I have goosebumps! And only one thing can settle them. Zaltzman. Kimber. Two Men Out. Get in here!  Okay, that doesn't make any sense. Bet the Two Men would be proud of me

"WI should consider asking Charles to keep the wickets tonight and strengthening their team with yet another fast bowling all rounder Holder by replacing their only weak link Ramdin." ---- Diagnosis noted, Dr. Tam. Can I get a lollipop now, please?

Dr. Tam: "I can give you the lollipop you deserve for such a nice coverage but first promise us an injection of boundaries and a syrup of absorbing cricket tonight?" ------ What makes you think I won't just say yes and steal my treat, just like that? I's a bad bad boy. 

5.55 pm The home team might not be here, but the buzz in Kolkata has been phenomenal. The pre-match press conference, for example, was teeming with journalists. England and West Indies have provided a story and a half for all of us to follow. One of redemption. One of rediscovery. One of youth. One of the spectacular. Well, maybe I might be misusing my creative licence a bit there, so let me cede the stage to Sidharth Monga, who has penned the preview for this match and the all the necessary numbers are sprawled in here with S Rajesh, waiting for you to join the party.

"We have a battle between two wonderful teams led by two under performing skippers. Sammy and Morgan will need to step up to be able to steal the glory tonight!" ---- But wouldn't you say they've made up for that with their leadership? The belief these two men have instilled in their team has been quite inspirational. 

"I am from that 1% who claimed Eng will win the WC and I still stand by it," Avinash has been putting time behind the crystal ball. Wonder if I should ask him about the lottery....

"Al, we need your expert opinion even before the match starts. Fantasy teams need to be updated. Pitch ? Dew ? Your thoughts?"  Oh Kamran, you have tears welling up in my eyes. Such a special feeling this. *Sniff* Well, lets see if I can help you out. Ummm.. Pitch you say? Sammy says all he wants is one 22 yards long and six feet wide. I'll go with that. While also mentioning Morgan had seen some grass in there. Mostly to hold it together and keep it firm. And dew... well, even without it, you'd fancy chasing here in Kolkata. Pack your team with batsmen, and good death bowlers. 

"It's hot and humid here in Kerala," and so Chukkan yelps, "Expecting Gayle Force 9." ---- Trust me, it won't cool things down. He's two short of becoming the first player ever to hit 100 T20I sixes. 

5.45 pm Would the women's triumph spur Darren Sammy and his men? They came out to celebrate with them, to soak in that winnin' feelin and to see if it might stick with them in a few hours' time. But England aren't the England of old. They've got Joe Root who gunned down 229 without batting en eyelid (while batting cricket balls out of Wankhede like they were ghosts and he was the answer to "who you gonna call?"). They've got Chris Jordan, who is pretty much a bot in human form programmed to bowl yorkers. They've got Eoin Morgan, who has been lauded for bringing sexy the fun back. England deserve their place in this World T20 final, and it makes it all the more sweeter because their limited-overs cricket was being skewered after their squeaky old World Cup. 

"Right, I've read everything, watched everything (including Jarrod and Mel- a lovely couple), made a comment or two. A quick look-in at the World Curling championships (you think cricket's a minority sport?) and I'll be ready to see England put another piece of silver on the mantelpiece where, let's face it, there's lots of room." John, you are a model student. Here you go, you can enjoy Ian Chappell's analysis where he puts his bowling cap on.  

"Hello from South Korea...," Welcome, Prashant. Put your feet up. There's nachos in the kitchen too. Oh, um.. actually, I finished it off. Oops. "Any news about pitch? 200+ score in Kolkata? Eagerly waiting for the clash of batting powers!" ---- It would seem we have a flat pitch to assist two teams with great power-hitting ability. So sit down, strap in and let's savour a final to remember. 

5.15 pm Shall we begin with a little bit of fun then? Nearly 40,000 people stopped by our poll asking who would win the World T20. West Indies got 6% votes and England, well, they got 1%. And here they are, at Eden Gardens, fighting to be called World Champions. It's like fate came up to us, pranced about, bopped us all on the nose and yelled "Gotcha!"

Oh, and for those rallying, champion-ing and variously supporting the West Indies, the women's team are breaking records and are on the cusp of taking the crown away from Australia. Haley Matthews - all of 18 years old - has blitzed them. And there it is! West Indies have won the Women's World T20. "#doingitinstyle" tweeted Brian Lara, and they've put away one of the two trophies up for grabs tonight. West Indies recorded the second-highest chase in Women's World T20 history thanks to their best first-wicket partnership in history. And the men have walked out onto the pitch to celebrate with their colleagues. Curtly Ambrose, Darren Sammy, Carlos Brathwaite, Andre Russell... 

Meanwhile, Meg Lanning and the Australians walk away in shock. The captain was down on the turf, needing help to be lifted up. They won this trophy three times - back to back to back - and now even after posting a substantial 148, they couldn't do much on a belter of a track. 

"I am rooting for red-hot England in this final," booms Prabhat. That's just the sort of gung ho we're looking for. "Roy has brought so much joy to start English innings with new dash of optimism that was leaking from England from few years,and,how better will it be,to win it against the most dangerous T20 outfit ever--WI.....May the best team win....Its definitely felt like Clash of Titans from my side..#feeling the heat."

"2 hours 50 minutes and counting: have you any idea how long it takes to chill a magnum of Perrier Jouet Grand Brut to 2 degrees Celsius?" Mr Confident has stumped me. Those pretty bails have lit up, but I will not move. Commentary referee, do your worst. 

Yep, this is probably the earliest you've ever seen anything in commentary but, hey, it's a big day and we've got loads of good stuff for you to read and watch in the build-up. From the England side, there is Andrew Miller on the class of 2016 v 2010 and Andrew Fernando on the team's new cloak. On the West Indies, meanwhile, Sid Monga delves into the team which is already well associated with the word 'Champion'. The captains, too, have had their say: Darren Sammy wanted to get something off his chest, while Eoin Morgan was soaking in England's remarkable turnaround. That's not all, though. You can also find out what our Match Day panel makes of the final and there's the latest edition of #politeenquires with Jarrod and Mel. Phew, that's probably enough for now. See you in the afternoon!

".....and this is probably the earliest interaction with you guys," Aww, dear Andrew Cowell: You missed us. "Right, T20. Hit and giggle it once was; morphed into an elder-statesmens retirement pay-day; administrators have tried to cash-in with non-cricket watchers; but now pretty much accepted alongside mainstream ODI's. This much we all know. Two previous winners meet: the mighty swinging Calypso bats against the guile of an all-bases-covered England. Fascinating stuff. The bookies can't split them. Here's hoping for a cracker....with an England smile at the end. May your fingers keep up with it all, gentlemen."

commentary: no need for the ump there! The slider goes straight through Roy. What a start for West Indies, and yet Badree barely celebrates. He just walks in to collect the applause like a boss. Another straighter one, pitches on middle, zips through to take leg. Roy was a bit too slow on it again, and played down the wrong line too.
tossed up on middle, Root, that charmingly clever batsman, simply pushes it down the ground
there won't be any turn with the new ball. It would just skid on. Hales is on the back foot, punches down the ground
beautiful batting! His feet are moving straight away - jumped back to take hold of a short ball and drills it through the covers.
flighted on middle and leg, serenely driven to long-on
ooooh, that wasn't pretty for England. Nerves apparent. Gets awayswing, and it draws Root into that backfoot punch. Except this is too wide of him and he can't reach it
pre_text: Vikrant Mahamun: "Okay! Now how many times do u see a team cheered as much as India even after knocking them out." ---- You'd suspect they might warm to Root too, considering his strokeplay. Here's Dre Russ with a slip

commentary: neatly behind it, and the sound off the bat is crisp. Drilled into the covers off the back foot
"yeah, yeah," Root yells looking for a second after a flick through midwicket. Had loads of time to play that despite Russell's rapid pace. Two was on offer, but Hales seems to have slipped
grabs the ball and gets in position to throw. "Yay," yells the crowd. Very coliseum like. Good length ball on off stump, pushed back at the bowler

he's picked out short fine leg! The only man there! Russell cannot believe it. Hales is livid with himself. This was a half-tracker, down the leg side, begging to be tonked and he simply helped it into the hands of Badree. A few yards either side, or even a little more height on that and England would have had the boundary they wanted to settle nerves
dismissal: AD Hales c Badree b Russell 1 (6m 3b 0x4 0x6) SR: 33.33

commentary: back of a length on off stump, defended
pre_text: Eoin Morgan in the second over, at his home ground from the IPL. He is greeted by two slips

commentary: strides out to meet a full delivery outside off and sends it to long-on
flighted outside off, Morgan jams a drive into the covers
comes forward on off stump and defends. Good accuracy from Badree
still no runs for the captain. This was a shade short and he went back to glide it past short third man, found the man instead
that one was faster. Lovely change of pace and Morgan, looking to back away, had to hurry into a push into the covers

was that the googly? Or did it just slide on? Morgan had not picked it, whichever it was. He was playing for the leggie, defending on middle when the ball pitched on off stump and went on into the keeper's gloves
goes back to a good length ball on off stump, pushed back at the bowler
pre_text: D.S.A: "@Muthu: Morgan actually plays for the SunRisers. Also, at this ground, he averages a mere 20. It hardly helps to have such experience, if that experience is hellish." ---- Ooopsy, guess I got a little too excited. West Indies went with one over spells till the ninth over in the semi-final. It continues. Benn is in. Slip in again

commentary: superbly played! That punch through the covers is too good. The high elbow, the little power he generates with his bottom hand as well. Was a poor ball - short and a tad wide - but Root took care of it so well
tossed up on off stump, driven down the ground
when in doubt, go over the infield! Morgan saw one in his area, strode forward and it was a good stride too, reached the pitch and lashed it over cover
flighted on off stump, driven to long-on
hit in the gap past mid-on! And that was because of his footwork again. This time he was lunging forward, took a flighted ball on the full and whipped it away. Top shot
pre_text: No slips now

commentary: they didn't go for an appeal, does that mean Morgan got something on his sweep. Morgan had moved across outside off to premeditate the shot. Seemed to strike in line, height might have been an issue?
moves away from a straight one on middle, sliced to point
he's messed that up. Badree doesn't often do that, but he gets away with it. A short ball zips past Morgan before he could cut it

the googly! This time it takes the outside edge and Gayle is there to gobble it up. It seems he hadn't picked this one either, judging from the way he had tried to close the bat face and was hoping to work a straight ball around the corner. The outside edge of doom!
dismissal: EJG Morgan c Gayle b Badree 5 (9m 12b 1x4 0x6) SR: 41.66

commentary: likes it when its tossed up, and its driven to mid-off
tried to beat mid-off on his left, but he hasn't put in enough power. Good control though. England need some of that right about now
and there it is. Off a shortish length, dabbed to short third man. Samuels misfields
pre_text: DJ Bravo's in, with one over left in the powerplay. Look out for that slower ball! Kolkata grooves"Dee-Jay, Dee-Jay, Dee-Jay!"---- That's catchy!

commentary: that's a poor one. Took all the pace off it, but he's also banged it in. Allowed Buttler ample time to see it and smite it over point.

he's picked another slowy! And this is the harder one - the one he puts full and makes it dip on the batsman - Buttler waits on it and whirls its wrist down on the ball. It screams away through midwicket, Russell is the man chasing it down, dives after the ball, but at the point where the ball makes contact with his left hand, his towel, stuck on his backside, seems to touch the rope. Or has it? It's tough to really say for sure. Probably safe. And safe it was
short again, and he swivels on his back foot and pulls to deep midwicket
perhaps waiting for the slower ball, Root's been done in by the normal one while going for a cut shot. Also seemed to indicate that it had stayed low. Interesting
neatly clipped off the middle stump to the left of deep square leg. Well, that was not the Powerplay England wanted.
fired in flat and quick just outside off, cut into the covers
pre_text: Badree to finish off

commentary: whipped away to wide long-on, where there is a misfield.
driven to long-on as Badree flights one in on off stump
stayed back to a good length ball, doesn't commit to it until it reaches him, that's when he knows it doesn't turn, and simply tucks it behind square leg
hammered away! This is a loopy old full toss on leg stump and Root jumps all over it and trampolines up and down yelling "wheee" for good measure. Whipped through midwicket
shortish and outside off, lurks deep in his crease and punches to the sweeper cover
that's too short and Root swivels on his back foot to pull along the ground to the left of deep backward square leg
pre_text: Naman: "I predict a 53 ball hundred for Buttler." ---- There we go. He's got 45 balls to make 91 runs! Here's big Carlos Brathwaite

commentary: goes wide of the crease for a back of a length ball, Root nudges it wide of long-on and looks for two. Not on offer
aimed a yorker, or rather aimed at Buttler's feet when he came down the pitch. Worked to long-on
good length ball on off stump, pushed into the covers and then asks for a change of gloves
that seems bread and butter for him, picks up the stray on the pads early, waits for it to come and uses the bowler's pace against him. Sweet flick to deep square leg
low full toss - is he going for the yorkers this early - steered to deep point
shortish and outside off, chopped to short third man
pre_text: DanielAlexander: "Will West Indies reclaim the No 1 spot in T20I rankings if they win today please?" ---- Apologies, I'm not quite sure of that yet. Will keep track of it though. Heeeeeer's Benny

commentary: tossed up on middle and leg, Buttler keeps to his crease and works it down to long-on
vast open spaces in front of square on the leg side with all three men on the boundary. Root looked at the acreage and clipped it through midwicket
phew! That was flat! Didn't look like it had any business going that far, bottom-hand shoveled it over extra cover and it kept gaining distance
gentle little clip between deep midwicket and long-on and they've raced across for a couple. Excellent work!
oh, heyo! That one grips and turns. Pitched outside leg, Buttler was ready for another whip, but seeing the ball deviate off the pitch, he blocks it
sits up for the pull shot, and he drags it from outside off to deep square leg. Brathwaite has a job on his hands, moving to his left and making sure his trousers don't fall off while he dives.
pre_text: Taha Sheikh: "The key wicket for WI here would be Root..He's playing very sensibly and has scored 31 off England's 57.." ---- Dre Russ is back

commentary: eased it behind point
back of a length and outside off, pushed through the covers
great composure under pressure. He has picked on every bad ball and sent it crying away to the boundary. This time the short one is pulled to long leg ever so easily. #ToughSituationBully?
pre_text: I haven't checked Vikas' numbers, but here they are: "@DanielAlexander: No they won't.. If WI wins they gain 2 points and it will take them to 125 and India are at 126 so they will be 2nd only even if they lose also.."

commentary: good length on middle, worked to the right of long-on. Root sprinted away, looking for more than the one run they get
aims for the blockhole, Buttler eases it through the covers.
into the crowd! This soared away, so high, so blindingly high. Buttler raced down the track and swung free. He was helped by the ball being in his arc.
pre_text: Raees Ul Haq: "Stokes and Ali to follow these two. Gearing up for 160+ . Rashid and Ali will be key if England is to win" ---- Okay, now that the sees sawed that far, who wants to guess which West Indies bowler pulls it back?

commentary: superb hitting! England are rolling now, this is an even better hit. Comes forward, while making some room, and lofts him over extra cover. Brave shot
shortish and outside off, hammered to deep point
pre_text: Sammy has a long chat with his bowler

commentary: flighted on off stump, driven to long-off.
whipped away through to deep midwicket, as Benn keeps bowling flat and quick after those two sixes
pushed through on off stump, driven into the covers to retain strike. That might be Benn's last of the night
slower ball comes out as a full toss, Boo, it says to Joe Root, who probably gives that naughty little grin and pats it to long-on

DJ's pumped up! Not sure his words are for the public, but he has taken a fine catch on the midwicket boundary. It was a back of a length ball that Buttler had picked up right off the middle. Crash, came the sound and the ball hurtled away flat. Right into the hands of the fielder
dismissal: JC Buttler c Bravo b Brathwaite 36 (29m 22b 1x4 3x6) SR: 163.63

commentary: good length ball on leg stump, whipped to deep midwicket and fresh legs mean they get across for a second
pre_text: Ben Stokes, he says he loves being in the middle in a pressure situation, instead of stuck fidgeting. Wide slip in

commentary: nicely sliced to deep cover
comes forward and takes a length ball on off stump and clips it towards long leg. He's playing a mighty little innings here
139 kph, wide yorker outside off, squeezed out to deep cover
pre_text: Slip's vanished

commentary: that's only his 13th ball of the tournament. Slower ball from around the stumps, driven to long-off

top-edge, off to the boundary. Almost! Benn pops a boot in front of it. This was a scary moment for Root. Came down the track, Sammy dragged it short, pull shot answered by he was beaten for pace. Lucky escape
and that's how he capitalises on it! How well did he wait on that. He knows he needs runs off the change-up bowler, he knows if he beats point, he gets some. And that's all he does
takes a slower ball from outside off and gives it a home at deep midwicket. Eden Gardens positively roars for Root's fifty
thumped away! That's the hundred! England have recovered and how. This is a belter of a pitch, and such balls - short and slow - are just desserts. Stokes hammers it away
two they want, and a mis-hit to long-on ends up in England's benefit
the slower ball is his stock ball, but when he puts it that short, it doesn't work. Root is not premeditating. This is pure instinct. Waits on the ball, on the front foot, and laces it past point
pre_text: Root surveys the field, counting the fielders down like Deadpool counted down his bullets

commentary: superb delivery! That's the loopy, dipping slower ball and Root is comfortably beaten. Seems only like an offcutter and it yet zings down at his pads. Root misses with the flick, Bravo appeals, but it was going down
looks for the yorker on leg stump, but it's not the right line. Whipped away to the left of deep square leg. Sammy is the man there, and he puts in the big boot

oh, what happened there?! Whatever did, Bravo and Gayle are 'champion'ing it together. It was perhaps the slower ball bouncer, Stokes was set up for the pull and then realised he would be beaten for pace. Decides to bail out of the shot, except the ball followed his moving away down leg. Leaps off the open face and ends up in point's hands. Dolly of a catch
dismissal: BA Stokes c Simmons b Bravo 13 (12m 8b 1x4 0x6) SR: 162.5

commentary: fuller ball outside off, goes for an on the up-drive, and is beaten
pre_text: Moeen Ali's the new man. who hit the winning runs in that chase agaisnt South Africa

commentary: strangled down leg! It's the slower ball again and Bravo's done the star turn for West Indies. Poor Root can only watch from the other end as the shortish delivery is gloved to the wicketkeeper. Out comes the champion dance again, this time Sammy and Bravo are doing it together as the team crowds around them
dismissal: MM Ali c †Ramdin b Bravo 0 (2m 2b 0x4 0x6) SR: 0

commentary: full and down leg, Root was looking at a flick to the fine leg boundary, doesn't connect
pre_text: And away Bravo goes to a boundary, and gets the crowd into the act. Explosion of noise at Eden. Chris Jordan is in, England six down. Root needs to go int overdrive

commentary: big Benn comes down and how! And Root's walking off with a volley at someone. He premeditated a scoop shot, moving outside off, so Brathwaite slowed it up and shortened the length. The batsman was left reaching for the ball up over his face, and without pace, he simply guides it to Benn at short fine leg
dismissal: JE Root c Benn b Brathwaite 54 (62m 36b 7x4 0x6) SR: 150

commentary: fuller ball outside off, driven to long-off.
pre_text: David Willey comes in at No. 9

commentary: fuller ball on off stump, defended to point
yorker on off stump, squeezed away to third man
yorker on middle, Jordan says pot calling kettle and blocks. Brathwaite claims the ball, and appeals for a catch. Nope. Not getting that
slower ball on off stump, turned away to long-on
pre_text: Eden are yelling Brathwaite's name too as Noman Awan reminds us: "110-4 111-7"

commentary: beaten for pace as Dre Russ bowls a short one on middle and leg. Stands there wondering where the ball went before listening to Willey and running across for a leg bye
pre_text: Last five overs then. England do bat deep, but Root's dismissal will hurt them badly here.

commentary: that's the offcutter slower ball, grips on the pitch and shaves past Willey's poke outside off. England will need to take note of that. Moeen, Rashid...
shortish and outside off, waft and miss from Willey
finally connects with the slowy, but the pull short to a short one finds short fine leg
that's at full pace, rearing up towards his face, Willy plays a flick more than a pull and finds a single to deep midwicket
low full toss on off stump, sent back down the pitch. That's only two runs off the over
full and wide, Willey steers it straight to point
pre_text: Sachin: "@crininfo team: u can say it this way "England do bat deep but not wide" it means they have 11 pinch hitters but not too many of them are proper batsmen. .. on a good day they can score @10RPO but on most of other days today's story gets repeated " ---- That's mighty harsh. Root played one of the innings of the tournament today. Just needed support

commentary: heaved away! He opens in domestic T20, remember! Dismantles a length ball over deep midwicket. Brathwaite was the man there - one of the tallest men positioned there to pull off the high catches, clever move - but it sails over him
works away to the man at square leg
drags a fuller ball from outside off and slogs it to wide long-on. Mis-hit actually, more of an inside edge. Russell's too quick to allow them a second
lands the yorker on middle and leg, jammed to long-on
pre_text: Paul Dawson: "I've not been able to follow this sorry story throughout the innings, but I don't recall seeing the initials KP anywhere. Have I missed something or are these initials banned?" ------ Oh, come now. Let's not open that can of worms. Around the stumps now

commentary: bang! That's 14 off the over, after just two off the last. England are still in this, and Willey believes. Takes a low full toss and hammers it down the ground
fuller ball on off stump, drilled to long-off
pre_text: Harbhajan Singh tweets: BADREE .You have set the example how to bowl on non spinning wickets.great spell at wankhede and today at Eden garden @qmanbad God bless u ----- Meanwhile, Brathwaite to bowl a pressure over. he's got 2 for 17 so far. Jordan can swing it...

commentary: belted down the ground. If you ever want to see pure power, that's it. It was a length ball, he was eager for it. Freed his arms and found his spot

he misjudged it at first, but Charles rushes forward and dives as far as he could to pick up the catch! Willey found a short ball and wanted to send it out of the park. But he was perhaps beaten for lack of pace. Hits him high on the bat and therefore ruins his timing
dismissal: DJ Willey c Charles b Brathwaite 21 (16m 14b 1x4 2x6) SR: 150

commentary: clipped to deep midwicket, Russell is over there, keeps it to a single
pre_text: Liam Plunkett is in at No. 10, not on strike

commentary: big appeal for lbw, and although it did seem adjacent and it hit him on the fulll, Plunkett had come down the track and the ball had plenty of distance to travel
full toss outside off, pushed into the covers. Brathwaite finishes up, with sweat pouring down. Takes high-fives from his captain after his 3 for 23
fuller ball outside off - and its that slow, dipping, deadly one - Plunkett, such a tall man, manages to get the bat down and skew it away through midwicket
swung out to deep square leg for a couple

he's taken the catch, but it seems like he has hurt his shoulder coming down to hit the turf. Badree was the man tracking down a cue-ender as Plunkett swung wildly. Moved to his right, dives full length, takes it in both hands, but he lands on his right wrist, even a bit of the shoulder. That could be dangerous, Badree's finished his quota today though
dismissal: LE Plunkett c Badree b Bravo 4 (4m 4b 0x4 0x6) SR: 100

commentary: big old slower ball, dipping on the batsman outside off, Rashid digs it out to point
pre_text: Adil Rashid is at No. 11. He has 10 first-class tons!

commentary: fuller ball, at full pace, at the base of off stump. Single into the covers.
slower ball taken from outside off and deposited at deep midwicket
pre_text: Syed Murtaza Ha: "Never noticed England has such a deep batting line up!"

commentary: fast, full and too quick for Rashid to connect. So they scamper a leg bye
pre_text: Final over of the innings.... England have managed only 35 runs in the five overs leading to this, and lost three wickets. Dre Russ it will be to round off

commentary: through him! That was the yorker, tailing in at the right-hander as he made room. Superb delivery. Great execution.
that's a vital hit! Jordan picks the gap at square leg, and he got a full toss to help him steal the boundary. Good batting.
shortish and outside off, pulled to long-on. Holder at long-on, subbing for Badree, can't stop a second
slogged away to deep midwicket, full toss again from Dre Russ

well stopped by Charles, saves two runs and England finish with a score that they can bowl at. Russell missed his spot again and Rashid smeared him to the right of the sweeper. Charles had to rush across and dive to save a boundary
pre_text: Sharif As-Saber: "For England, making a 150 may be a difficult task now but still would love to see the final tail twisting by Rashid and Jordan!" ---- They've got more than that!

commentary: angled across from over the wicket, decent length and Charles patiently waits, steers to point
pre_text:
David Willey will take the new ball, Charles on strike. Off go the fireworks on the boundary's edge - lights, camera, action!

England are having a cuddle on the outfield. They're probably feeling a bit bruised... Here come Chris Gayle and Johnson Charles, the noise in the crowd rising with them. Samuel Badree, meanwhile, is holding an ice pack to his shoulder in the dugout.

Ahoy there, me hearties - and thanks for a super spell, Al No1. Does England's total amount to a hill of beans? Can the bowlers make West Indies fight for their right to party tonight? We were expecting some "Boom boom!" but it might be a short recital, if Chris Gayle gets going against his favourite opponent. Then again, this isn't so bad, as World T20 final scores go (batting first, anyway) - England finished a couple shy of the total India defended in 2007. What chance another thriller in Kolkata?

Nasir Shahnawaz is pointing to precedent: "We not need to forget that West Indies have lost from Afghanistan due to their overconfidence. "

"I reckons England is in big trouble as they are already 10-20 runs short and their bowling is not good at start of the inning which is very necessary when you are defending less than 160 and there is players like Chris Gayle." Sanketp45 puts it another way.

"All aboard the Stokes train, right Alan?" Start shoveling coal, Hoover... Toot, toot!

commentary: fuller and straight, 131kph/81mph and shaping a fraction to hit the pads and roll to short midwicket
pitched up and curling back on off stump, this time Charles bunts it back down the track
full again, on off stump and driven with stiff hands, briefly in the air but bouncing short of mid-off
on the legs, Charles plays across the line... and does he get a touch on that? Buttler goes up for the catch behind but Rod Tucker decides, correctly, that it flicked the pad on its way through
pitched full on middle and leg, this time he times a glance through backward square to get the WI score up and running

round the wicket, dollied on the stumps.... and he skies a catch to mid-on! Stokes settled safely under it and England's funky cricket brings them an early reward. Huge yahoo from Charles, who's not subtle at the best of times, straight up and down and he's back in the hutch for spit
pre_text: Hello, what's this... Morgan rolls the dice and gives Joe Root the second over
dismissal: J Charles c Stokes b Root 1 (4m 7b 0x4 0x6) SR: 14.28

commentary: tossed up outside off, carved over point, thick outside edge from Gayle but it clears the ring and outruns two players to the rope
pre_text: Marlon Samuels out at No. 3... and the World Boss on strike

commentary: slogged into the sky - straight to long-off! Root has two in the over, and CHRIS GAYLE IS OUT! He's gone one better than Kohli already, Gayle was looking to bludgeon the ball into the stands over long-off, as he has done so many times to so many offspinners, but he got slightly under it, sliced towards "Safe Hands" Stokes running round to his right... and he's mobbed by his team-mates! Root is bellowing in celebration, England have landed a huge blow in this final
dismissal: CH Gayle c Stokes b Root 4 (8m 2b 1x4 0x6) SR: 200

commentary: floated up on off stump, pushed back to the bowler
pre_text: Samuels on strike then, slip in

commentary: full on the pads and this is clipped calmly through midwicket, between two fielders and away for four
flighted, Samuels drills it into the ground, Root gets a hand on it jumping up but can't prevent them from running
fullish around off stump, driven back to the bowler
pre_text: My word, what a start... Any Beliebers out there now? Lendl Simmons, who's coming in to this game on the back of some form, is the other new man

commentary: goes across and steers the ball towards backward point for one
pre_text: "Oh What Game!!!! Hold your breath....." gulps Noman Awan

commentary: straightening, struck on the pads in front of leg stump - given! Yoinks, this is a sensational start from England! Was that a touch high? Rod Tucker didn't think so and Simmons is gone for a golden duck! Pitched in line with middle and leg, hurtled on to hit the pads - and Hawk-Eye has it hitting the top of the stumps! England are cock-a-hoop (and that's not a Willey pun)
pre_text: "Yep! Its Root=Kohli!" chirps Kozhi kanniampu
dismissal: LMP Simmons lbw b Willey 0 (5m 1b 0x4 0x6) SR: 0

commentary: touch short, shuffles across and glances the ball through backward square leg
pre_text: In comes DJ Bravo... WI in need of a champion

commentary: good length, angled across, Samuels coolly, calmly dabs the ball down behind point
pushed across in the channel outside off, Bravo watches it through. WI just need to take a moment, here
length ball in the corridor outside off, goes back and across and dabs the ball through backward point
pre_text: Chris Jordan replaces the golden boy

commentary: shortish, over off stump, Bravo whips his hands through a pull through midwicket for one
back of a length outside off, steered down to third man, they think better of trying for two
pre_text: Morgan is looking ice cool in the field... Poor with the bat but he's earning his corn now

commentary: cracked into the covers off the back foot, excellent bit of fielding prevents one. Jordan up at 88mph with that delivery
banged in short, feisty little bumper from Jordan, rearing at the throat, Bravo does well to fend to the leg side and into a gap
outside off stump, touch short and guided away for one off the back foot again
dug in back of a length, Samuels looks hurried by the extra pace, blocks in front of middle and leg
pre_text: Another change from Morgan, Liam Plunkett on

commentary: fired in with the arm from over the wicket, turned to midwicket, another dot
continues to hammer away back of a length, this time in the channel, Samuels makes room but punches to cover point
shortish, at the body, nudged fine of the man on the edge of the circle for one
up at 148kph/92mph this delivery, short and Bravo manages to tuck it off his hip into a gap
pre_text: "This is how a final should be.. Finals shouldn't be a canter.. Earn the cup!!" Someone is going to have to, Sharad

commentary: back of a length, hitting 145kph/90mph again, worked through the leg side - just three singles off the over
first boundary since the second over, short ball and swatted away through midwicket, smoothly done by Samuels, rocking back and rolling the wrists
dug in, Samuels swings with abandon... and top-edges over the keeper for four more! Not where he was aiming but it scoots away, back-to-back boundaries
shortish outside off, steps away and slaps into the covers, half stopped but that diverts it away from mid-off, who has to chase it towards the rope
lasered through the covers, stunningly good stroke! Touch too full, outside off and Samuels breezes it past the infield, they barely had time to move
Jordan, forced wide of the stumps, concedes an extra...
pitched up on off stump, drops the bat and digs it out into the covers
full outside off again, Samuels plays that flowing back-foot drive he is so adept at, picks up another single in front of square

wafts outside off, thin nick... did that carry? Yes! Looked like a slower ball from Plunkett, airy swipe from Samuels and West Indies' brief recovery is checked. Hang on, they are going to check this after all. I don't think this will be given, looks like it bounced off the tips of Buttler's gloves, on to the turf and then back up. Samuels had sloped most of the way to the boundary but he is now making a more purposeful walk back. Right decision made
pre_text: Liam Plunkett continues

commentary: sharp from Plunkett, the follow up rapping Samuels on the gloves, punched away to backward point
Plunkett still pushing the pace up above 90mph drops back and glides one to third man
angled in with the arm, Bravo hops across and stabs into the leg side
dug in short, rising towards the arm pit, does well to ride the bounce and turn one to midwicket
tight lines, absolutely no width, arrowing in on the stumps, Samuels can only push it back to the bowler - excellent stuff from Plunkett, despite the disappointment of missing out on a wicket
pushed through on off stump, nicely bowled and pushed back down the track
pre_text: Right, back to spin, Adil Rashid and a big test for England's resolve... Can they stop WI hitting boundaries?

commentary: spin for Rashid, this ripped from leg to off, dipping and turning past the outside edge... That'll have England interested
tossed up on the stumps, worked for one through midwicket
pre_text: Morgan brings in a slip

commentary: pushed through, flat legbreak on middle and leg, pushed down the ground
quicker ball, I think, stays back and jabs it through square leg
dragged down, Samuels stays in the crease and swats one more down the ground - tidy start from the England leggie
pre_text: There's the mother of all Mexican waves sweeping around Eden Gardens right now...

commentary: full and sliding towards the pads, Samuels gets a chunk of bat on it and sends the ball whistling through backward square leg for a welcome boundary
pre_text: "One does not simply underestimate England's death bowling nor does one underestimate West Indies chasing." It's boiling up nicely then, Sam

commentary: back of a length outside off, squeezed towards point
pitched up outside off, waits for it, waits for it, waits for it... and punches behind square
loses line, down the leg side
back of a length outside off, Bravo goes across and defends square
dug in, rising towards the boat race, Bravo fends it away into the leg side for one
Plunkett peppering the middle of the pitch, Samuels tries to make room but bottom edges a swipe down into the turf
tossed up around off stump, driven through the covers for a single
pre_text: "I simply can´t understand people holding tickets for the final and not showing up just because the hosts gone out in the semis... What a waste ! It´s a final after all so why give the tickets back ??? Cherish the sport !!" Well, it's not been the pinnacle of organisation this tournament, Robert... Why change now?

commentary: googly from Rashid, nearly foxes Samuels, he plays the wrong line and gets an inside edge
flighted, shuffles out this time, pushes one back down the ground
goes for the big shot, tossed up enticingly, Bravo heaves to leg but mistimes it for one
pushed through on off, another googly that Samuels doesn't seem to read
flat, a touch quicker, drops back outside off and steers one more through backward point
that will help settle WI, four off the first ball, a languid stroke through backward point, beats third man
pre_text: Halfway stage, the RR now above 10 for the first time... Ben Stokes on to bowl

commentary: good pace, 141kph/88mph from Stokes, punched back to the bowler in his follow through
bouncer, maybe taking the pace off... but it veers down the leg side
length delivery outside off, rolls his fingers over the ball, Samuels waits and chops it through point
up towards the blockhole, Bravo is on is toes and connects sweetly with a leg glance, straight to the man on the fence
pre_text: "This is the situation of WI when there are 4 overs of Stokes and 2 overs of Jordan still to come," chin-strokes Rahul. "Nicely poised this game."

commentary: full outside the line of off, Samuels was waiting for the cutter and brought his bat down too late as the ball skidded through
on the stumps, 115kph/71mph as Stokes takes pace off again, Samuels steers it to backward point
tossed up on the stumps, drilled back down the ground for one
length ball, spinning away outside off, cut through point to the sweeper
pre_text: The remarkable thing is England have kept WI to just seven boundaries so far... But will the dam break?

commentary: gives it some air, dipping and miscued back to the bowler, along the ground
picks the googly this time, rocks on to the back foot and pulls between deep midwicket and long-on, just the single, however
pushed through on the stumps, Bravo tries to give it some humpty inside out, thick-edges into the leg side
flighted on off, driven with a flourish and they take on mid-off's arm... direct hit but Samuels was home
back of a length, maybe a slower ball, Samuels nonchalantly swats one through point
pre_text:
Stokes continues against his old mucker

The asking rate ticks above 11... Nurse! I can feel the visions starting!

commentary: Stokes loses it here, fired down wide of the stumps and seaming almost off the cut strip
full and straight, up in the blockhole, Bravo helicopters it but fails to gain any altitude, straight to mid-on and quickly, too, so no time to run

on the pull, top-edged out towards deep backward square leg... but Billings slips as he runs around and drops the chance! It bounces for four, too, to sharpen Stokes' frustration. He seemed to be underneath the ball but his momentum took him a bit beyond, then he lost his footing and the ball burst through and away
pitched up, squeezed out into the covers for one
pitched full and straight and dug out into the leg side
pre_text: Stokes is wiping his hands as he walks back to his mark - sweat, or dew?

commentary: fires it in full again, bunted towards mid-on and Root has a shy, needed a direct hit, Stokes couldn't quite grab it... and then Bravo collides with him as he charges through the crease. Everyone okay, though
tossed up and driven down the ground to long-on
pre_text: Rashid to bowl out his overs... WI need someone to hit the gas here

commentary: gives it some air, on off stump, Samuels strokes one through the covers
pre_text: Here's Steve: "Clever drop from Billings... Bravo's scoring slowly. Keeps Russell and Sammy out a while longer"

commentary: tossed up, on the stumps... and this is in the stands! WI finally flex their six packs, a muscle-bound mow across the line and it sails well beyond the ropes at deep midwicket for the first maximum of the WI innings
flighted legbreak, on off stump, comes forward and pushes into the covers
drops back outside off, steers one to backward point - Samuels raises his bat in a WT20 final for the second time, he's gluing the Windies innings together here

pushed through a touch quicker, Bravo swivels and attempts to plant Rashid in the stands again... but instead the top edge plops into the hands of backward point! Rashid strikes with his final ball, but it's probably not the man England wanted
dismissal: DJ Bravo c Root b Rashid 25 (53m 27b 1x4 1x6) SR: 92.59

commentary: gets one away to the boundary from the first ball, backing away and hoicked over mid-on and it has enough to beat long-on running across
pre_text: Liam Plunkett replaces Stokes

commentary: Samuels steps outside leg, Plunkett goes full and follows him, swiped through midwicket
back of a length over the top of off stump, Russell shows it a Test-match straight bat in defence
pre_text: "With Russell in now it will feel more like a t20 match." About time, eh, Zeeshan

commentary: drops back and dabs behind point, Roy pounces on it, collects and swivels to throw in one movement, but misses the stumps
full length, not quite full enough though... it's up towards the blockhole but Samuels gets under the ball and levers it up and over long-on for another six
mullered back down the ground! WI warming to their task, Samuels turning the heat up on Plunkett, who missed his yorker by inches again and saw it brutalised back over his head

dug in short, Russell pirouettes on the spot - but sends a pull straight into the hands of Stokes on the deep midwicket boundary! Willey pulls out a pair of imaginary pistols and starts shooting off bottle tops... He was trying to clear the boundary on the longest side of the ground, middled the shot but found Stokes running in to stoop and conquer
pre_text: David Willey returns, five overs to go, WI needing 52 more
dismissal: AD Russell c Stokes b Willey 1 (7m 3b 0x4 0x6) SR: 33.33

commentary: touch short, down the leg side
pre_text: Here's the captain, Darren Sammy... He's only faced 11 balls in the tournament to date

commentary: short, angled across in the channel, Sammy waits on it and carves over point, they charge back for two

goes for the big shot - AND HOLES OUT TO DEEP COVER! Sammy keeps up his Invisible Man routine, and you have to say that was not a sensible shot, only his third ball, a man standing out there, and he's picked him out. England are not letting go here
dismissal: DJG Sammy c Hales b Willey 2 (3m 2b 0x4 0x6) SR: 100

commentary: tries to dab the ball past short third man, the ball is fielded and Brathwaite has gone charging down... needed a harder, flatter throw to put him in trouble
pre_text: Willey pulled out the champion dance this time... Carlos Brathwaite is in, Samuels on strike

commentary: cut away, nicely placed behind the man on the boundary... but Alex Hales this time pulls off a brilliant sliding stop to prevent four
loses his line, behind Samuels legs
length delivery on the stumps, Samuels nurdles one more through midwicket
full length, wide of the stumps, Samuels drills it to cover, who has a throw at the non-striker's end - steady
pre_text: WI need 45 from 24, it's in their range but only four wickets are standing. Chris Jordan returns. England want - need - yorkers. This is the crunch, folks

commentary: pitched up, not quite there and it's smeared down the ground, Samuels lands a blow, whacked straight back from where it came
follows him as he steps to leg, swings hard and squeezes out one to midwicket
Jordan fires the ball in full outside off, Brathwaite is waiting, he sets himself to drive inside out and hammers it... but a brilliant diving stop at cover keeps them to one
goes full and even wider, Samuels was set to the leg side, swings and misses
unerring stuff from Jordan, dug out towards mid-on, again the throw comes in - would Samuels have made it? Jordan couldn't gather, but it would have been close
starts with a full toss, bunted down the ground for a couple
pre_text: David Willey stays on, so Stokes won't bowl out. Morgan has a hunch... 38 off 18

commentary: pitched up, on the stumps, swats at it and the ball deflects off the pads for a leg bye
fullish around off stump, Brathwaite makes room to hit over cover, gets a good connection... but Moeen pulls of a terrific running stop on the boundary to prevent four
pitched up, as it has to be, squeezed off the legs and Willey hares after it, slides and throws... Misses but it's just a single for WI
pre_text: And still the rate rises...

commentary: superb yorker from Willey, full on leg stump, can only squirt one to backward point
scooped for four to long stop! Brilliantly done from Brathwaite, with the pressure mounting, head down moving across his stumps, got the ramp in position and got it away for four
smashed down the ground, Samuels clears the infield and there is no one at long-off to cut it off!
pre_text: Jordan to bowl, West Indies need one of their cannons to fire at the last again...

commentary: full outside off, this time Samuels can't get under it, one down the ground
pre_text:
Long-off goes out now

Rahul: "India was in similar situation against Australia and Kohli pulled that off. Can Samuels will do something like Kohli? Difference was number of wickets."

commentary: Jordan holds his nerve, hurls down another thunder bolt, squeezed into the covers for one
goes full on leg stump as Samuels moves to leg, punches one down the ground to long-on
pre_text: "I still see Samuels century!" Cripes, Shahzad, he's closing in... This is now the highest individual score in a WT20 final. But will it be on the winning side?

commentary: hits his mark again, full on off stump, sliced over the covers and it's just one
pre_text: England leave fine leg back for Brathwaite and his ice cream scoop... 20 off eight

commentary: dot ball, squeezed under Samuels' bat! Full and wide and just what England desperately needed - Samuels loses the strike and WI will need to find the ropes in the final over!
Brathwaite starts the over with a six! Poor ball from Stokes, half-volley on leg stump, Brathwaite heaves across the line and clears the rope at deep backward square leg
pre_text: So, it's come to this. The final over, the reckoning. WI need 19 off six balls... This is it, folks. Time for a hero

commentary: smeared over long-on, back-to-back sixes from Brathwaite! The crowd are going nuts, Stokes looks shellshocked, again it wasn't quite full enough and he rammed it back over long-on
pre_text: That brings it down to 13 from five...

commentary: SIX MORE! Would you believe it? You had better believe it! West Indies are doing a jig in the dugout, not quite the "Champion" dance but they are pretty much there... That looked like a mishit but it sailed several metres back over long-off this time
pre_text: Forget a Hussey, a Brathwaite might do... 7 from four now

commentary: finishes it with a six! The most amazing final over and West Indies are World T20 champions for the second time! Stokes goes the distance, he's out on his feet and the West Indies players are out on the field, charging for the middle - this soared into the stands at deep midwicket and Brathwaite let out a primeval roar before being hugged by his team-mate Samuels
